record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a finitely presented group that is not sofic, meaning a group for which no sequence of maps into symmetric groups simultaneously makes every defining relation asymptotically hold in normalized Hamming distance while keeping every nontrivial word uniformly far from the identity permutation?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3 (Gromov [Gro99], Weiss [Wei00]). Are there non-sofic groups?

Definition 6.2. A finitely presented group Γ ∼= hS|Ri is said to be sofic if there is a sequence of functions fn : S → Sym(n), such that
∀r ∈ R : dh(fn(r),Id) n→∞ −−−→ 0,
and for every w /∈ hhRii,
lim inf(dh(fn(w),Id)) ≥ 1/2.

artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a non-sofic group (finitely presented or otherwise) is widely regarded as a major open problem, originally raised by Gromov and Weiss. Recent surveys and research papers (e.g., 2023–2024 work on sofic approximations of non-amenable groups) continue to treat it as unresolved.
